title: Stamp feature and cell onto the activity record so a session file answers what is being worked on
action: Extend the activity object written by hooks/activity.rs (per D2, additive) with two optional fields resolved at every write, fail-open (absent when unknown, never an error): `feature` — the session record's own `lane` field when present, else the `feature` of <control_root>/.bee/state.json; `cell` — the cell id of the ACTIVE claim held by this session_id: scan <control_root>/.bee/claims/*.json the way status_full/cells.rs active_workers does (read_claim + is_claim_active around its lines 743-765; claims_dir there; prompt_context.rs has a lenient reader near its line 1023/1726 you may reuse), pick the claim whose `session` equals the session_id, take its `cell`. Keep both reads cheap: one readdir of claims, no cell files opened. Write them into both the json `activity` object and each jsonl transition row. A feature/cell change alone (state unchanged) refreshes the json but is not a transition. Unit tests in the existing tests module: lane-bound session yields feature from lane; unbound yields state.json feature; an active claim yields cell, an expired or foreign claim yields no cell; no claims dir is fine. Update docs/knowledge/areas/hook-runtime/agent-activity-record.md field table with the two fields and their sources. Commit with trailer `cell: aah-4`.

truths: a session bound to a lane writes activity.feature = that lane
a session holding an active claim writes activity.cell = that cell id
a missing claims dir or unreadable claim never changes the exit code or blocks the state write

artifacts.substantive: feature and cell resolution wired into the activity write, with tests

key_links: the claim scan uses the same activity rule status active_workers uses (is_claim_active)
prohibitions: no change to the state machine or sticky rules
no new session-record fields outside activity
